clock_domain.anchors: request-independent monotonic_before_ns/unix_ns/monotonic_after_ns records with source, process, container and host identity plus sequence and previous hash
clock_domain.comparison: OTLP and Triton Unix-nanosecond actor starts and PostgreSQL database times are projected only through run-level anchor uncertainty envelopes
clock_domain.fail_closed: anchor width, gap, drift, source mismatch, overlapping causal intervals, phase Unix-to-monotonic mismatch, or any per-request self-derived offset

crossover_request.selection: one Blue hold request ID and nonce are deterministically fixed before dispatch
crossover_request.receipt_identity: attempt, run, request, nonce, trace, effect, model role/name/version/artifact, generation, actor and source identity
crossover_request.receipt_rule: each actor start is captured in raw actor evidence, committed to the existing PostgreSQL transactional store causal sequence, and independently read back

durable_terminal_effect.commit_order: inference result and hold complete after switch; terminal entity, idempotency response, and durable_terminal_effect causal receipt are committed in one synchronous_commit=on transaction; COMMIT ACK and independent readback precede response success
durable_terminal_effect.ordering: switch upper bound is strictly before durable effect commit lower bound; durable effect commit/readback precedes controller/server end and client completion
durable_terminal_effect.timestamp_claim: database_recorded_at plus commit ACK and independent readback form a conservative causal interval; no exact PostgreSQL commit instant is claimed

pre_unload.rule: the same PostgreSQL causal fence compares the complete pre-switch Blue server-entry identity set with terminal-effect receipts and rejects unload until every completion/effect is committed and visible
pre_unload.ordering: the unload-intent sequence follows all pre-switch Blue terminal-effect sequences; physical unload starts only after the unload-intent COMMIT ACK and readback

route_switch.fence: one serialized PostgreSQL transaction locks and validates the three crossover start receipts and their exact identities, then appends the switch event to the same causal sequence
route_switch.ordering: raw actor start upper bound is at or before receipt database record; every receipt COMMIT ACK and readback is strictly before switch commit lower bound
route_switch.runtime_rule: the controller cannot apply the Blue-to-Green route generation until the switch fence commit is acknowledged and independently visible

implementation_constraint.postgresql: reuse TransactionalControlPlaneStore in the isolated S6B-M schema; SET LOCAL synchronous_commit=on; no global PostgreSQL setting or restart
implementation_constraint.triton: accepted runtime is forbidden unless official raw Triton trace binds COMPUTE_START to the predetermined request nonce and exact model identity

supersession: the v4 contract remains immutable historical input; this amendment is mandatory and narrows accepted execution
trigger: runtime design review found that dual-clock anchors and terminal effects alone did not causally fence route switch on visible API, controller and Triton backend starts
